p.src: Zheng Kangcheng’s personal name was Xuan. A learned and gifted man, he had once studied under Ma Rong. Whenever Ma Rong lectured, he would set up a crimson curtain, gather his pupils before it, and place singing girls behind it, with maidservants arrayed on either side. For three years Zheng Xuan listened to his lectures without once casting an improper glance, and Ma Rong marveled greatly at him. When Zheng Xuan completed his studies and returned home, Ma Rong sighed, “Only Zheng Xuan has mastered the secrets of my learning!” Even the maidservants in Zheng Xuan’s household were all versed in the Mao recension of the Book of Songs. Once a maid offended Zheng Xuan, and he ordered her to kneel for a long while before the steps. Another maid teasingly quoted to her, “What are you doing there in the mud?” The kneeling maid answered at once, “I merely went to make complaint, and met with his anger.” Such was the literary refinement of his household. During Emperor Huan’s reign, Zheng Xuan rose to the office of Imperial Secretary. Later, amid the disorder caused by the Ten Regular Attendants, he abandoned office and retired to the countryside, settling in Xu Province. When Xuande was in Zhuo Commandery, he had already studied under him. After becoming Governor of Xu Province, Xuande frequently visited his dwelling to seek instruction and treated him with exceptional reverence.

p.src: The adviser Tian Feng said, “War has continued year after year; the people are exhausted and the granaries hold no reserves. We must not raise another great army. We should first send a man to present news of our victories to the Emperor. If he is denied passage, then submit a memorial declaring that Cao Cao has barred our road to the throne. After that, lead the army to encamp at Liyang, increase the number of boats and oars in Henei, repair and prepare our weapons, and dispatch picked troops separately to garrison the frontiers. Within three years, the great enterprise can be settled.” The adviser Shen Pei said, “That is not so. With Your Lordship’s divine prowess and the strength and prosperity of the lands north of the Yellow River under your command, raising an army against the traitor Cao will be as easy as turning one’s hand. Why delay for months and years?” The adviser Ju Shou said, “The means to victory do not lie in strength and numbers alone. Cao Cao’s laws and commands are firmly enforced, and his soldiers are well trained. He is not like Gongsun Zan, who sat passively and allowed himself to be besieged. To discard the sound plan of reporting our victories and instead raise an army without just cause is, in my humble opinion, a course Your Lordship should not adopt.” The adviser Guo Tu said, “No. How could attacking Cao Cao be called a war without just cause? Your Lordship should seize the moment and settle the great enterprise without delay. I urge you to follow Imperial Secretary Zheng’s advice, join Liu Bei in upholding righteousness, and destroy the traitor Cao. Above, this accords with Heaven’s will; below, it accords with the people’s desires. It would truly be a blessing beyond measure!”

p.src: The four men argued without reaching a decision, and Yuan Shao wavered, unable to choose. Suddenly Xu You and Xun Chen entered from outside. Yuan Shao said, “These two possess much insight. Let us hear what course they advocate.” After the two had paid their respects, Yuan Shao said, “Imperial Secretary Zheng has sent a letter urging me to raise an army, aid Liu Bei, and attack Cao Cao. Should I raise the army? Or should I not?” The two answered in unison, “Your Lordship can overcome the few with the many and attack the weak with the strong. To punish a traitor to the Han and uphold the imperial house, you should raise the army.” Yuan Shao said, “Your views accord perfectly with my own heart.” He then began discussing the mobilization of the army. First he ordered Sun Qian to return and report to Zheng Xuan, while arranging for Xuande to prepare to support the campaign. At the same time, he appointed Shen Pei and Pang Ji to command the army; Tian Feng, Xun Chen, and Xu You as advisers; and Yan Liang and Wen Chou as generals. He mustered one hundred and fifty thousand cavalry and the same number of infantry—three hundred thousand picked troops in all—and advanced toward Liyang.

p.src: Yuan Shao was delighted when he read the proclamation. He immediately ordered messengers to circulate it throughout the provinces and commanderies and post it at every pass, ferry, and strategic defile. When the proclamation reached the capital at Xu, Cao Cao was suffering from severe headaches and lay ill in bed. His attendants brought the proclamation in to him. At the sight of it, Cao Cao’s hair stood on end and cold sweat covered his body. Suddenly his headache vanished; he leapt from the bed and turned to Cao Hong. “Who wrote this proclamation?” he asked. Cao Hong replied, “I hear it is the work of Chen Lin.” Cao Cao laughed. “Skill in letters must be supported by military strategy. Chen Lin may excel with the pen, but what can he do about Yuan Shao’s deficiency in warcraft?” He then assembled his advisers to discuss how to meet the enemy.

p.src: When Kong Rong heard of it, he came to see Cao Cao and said, “Yuan Shao’s power is great. You must not fight him; peace is the only course.” Xun Yu said, “Yuan Shao is a man of no ability. Why even discuss peace?” Kong Rong said, “Yuan Shao’s lands are broad and his people strong. Among his subordinates, Xu You, Guo Tu, Shen Pei, and Pang Ji are all men of wisdom and strategy; Tian Feng and Ju Shou are both loyal ministers; Yan Liang and Wen Chou are the bravest men in all his armies; and the others—Gao Lan, Zhang He, Chunyu Qiong, and their peers—are all celebrated generals of the age. How can you call Yuan Shao a man of no ability?” Xun Yu laughed. “Yuan Shao has many troops, but they lack discipline. Tian Feng is unyielding and affronts his superiors; Xu You is greedy and unwise; Shen Pei is overbearing and devoid of strategy; Pang Ji is rash and useless. These men cannot possibly tolerate one another and will surely bring about internal strife. Yan Liang and Wen Chou possess only the courage of common fighting men; they can be captured in a single battle. As for the remaining mediocrities, even if there were a million of them, they would scarcely be worth mentioning!”

p.src: Kong Rong fell silent. Cao Cao laughed heartily. “None of them lies beyond Wenruo’s reckoning.” He then summoned Liu Dai of the vanguard and Wang Zhong of the rear army, ordering them to lead fifty thousand troops under the Prime Minister’s banners to Xu Province and attack Liu Bei. Liu Dai had formerly been Inspector of Yan Province. When Cao Cao took the province, Liu Dai surrendered to him, and Cao Cao made him a subordinate general. For this reason, he now sent Liu Dai to command the force together with Wang Zhong. Cao Cao himself led a great army of two hundred thousand to Liyang to oppose Yuan Shao. Cheng Yu said, “I fear Liu Dai and Wang Zhong are unequal to their commission.” Cao Cao replied, “I too know they are no match for Liu Bei. For the present, they are merely to make an imposing show.” He instructed them, “Do not advance rashly. Wait until I have defeated Yuan Shao; then I shall bring the army to destroy Liu Bei.” Liu Dai and Wang Zhong departed with their troops. Cao Cao personally led his army to Liyang. The two armies encamped eighty li apart, each digging deep moats and raising high ramparts. They faced one another without giving battle. The standoff lasted from the eighth month until the tenth. Xu You resented Shen Pei’s command of the army, while Ju Shou was bitter that Yuan Shao had rejected his counsel. The factions were at odds and made no effort to advance. Yuan Shao’s heart was full of doubt, and he gave no thought to advancing. Cao Cao therefore summoned Zang Ba, a surrendered general formerly under Lü Bu, and ordered him to guard Qing and Xu provinces; Yu Jin and Li Dian were stationed with troops along the Yellow River; and Cao Ren was given overall command of the main army and encamped at Guandu. Cao Cao himself took one army and returned directly to the capital at Xu.

p.src: Thereupon Yunchang led three thousand troops out of Xuzhou. It was early winter. Dark clouds massed overhead and snowflakes whirled wildly as both armies formed their ranks beneath the falling snow. Yunchang galloped forth with blade in hand and loudly called on Wang Zhong to parley. Wang Zhong rode out and said, “The Chancellor has come in person. Why do you not surrender?” Yunchang said, “Ask the Chancellor to come before the lines. I have something to say to him.” Wang Zhong said, “How could the Chancellor deign to meet you so lightly?” Yunchang flew into a rage and spurred his horse forward. Wang Zhong leveled his spear and rode to meet him. As their horses crossed, Yunchang wheeled his mount and fled. Wang Zhong pursued him. Once they had rounded a hillside, Yunchang turned his horse, gave a mighty shout, and came straight at him with his blade whirling. Unable to withstand him, Wang Zhong had just managed to spur his horse into flight when Yunchang reversed his precious blade into his left hand, seized the cord of Wang Zhong's armor with his right, dragged him from the saddle, laid him crosswise over his horse, and returned to his own lines. Wang Zhong's troops scattered and fled in all directions.

p.src: Now Liu Dai, learning that Wang Zhong had been captured, held firmly within his camp and refused to come out. Every day Zhang Fei hurled abuse before the camp. When Liu Dai learned that it was Zhang Fei, he became still more afraid to emerge. After waiting several days without Liu Dai appearing, Zhang Fei devised a plan. He issued orders to raid the camp at the second watch that night; during the day, however, he drank in his tent and feigned drunkenness, found fault with a soldier, had him severely beaten and bound within the camp, and declared, “When I lead out the troops tonight, I shall sacrifice him to the banner!” But in secret he ordered his attendants to let the man escape. Once free, the soldier stole out of the camp and went straight to Liu Dai's camp to report the planned night raid. Seeing that the supposed deserter was badly wounded, Liu Dai believed his story. He left an empty camp as a decoy and concealed his troops outside it.

u.src: Now Liu Dai, learning that Wang Zhong had been captured, held firmly within his camp and refused to come out.
Every day Zhang Fei hurled abuse before the camp. When Liu Dai learned that it was Zhang Fei, he became still more afraid to emerge.

After waiting several days without Liu Dai appearing, Zhang Fei devised a plan. He issued orders to raid the camp at the second watch that night; during the day, however, he drank in his tent and feigned drunkenness, found fault with a soldier, had him severely beaten and bound within the camp, and declared, “When I lead out the troops tonight, I shall sacrifice him to the banner!”
But in secret he ordered his attendants to let the man escape.
Once free, the soldier stole out of the camp and went straight to Liu Dai's camp to report the planned night raid.
Seeing that the supposed deserter was badly wounded, Liu Dai believed his story. He left an empty camp as a decoy and concealed his troops outside it.

p.src: That night Zhang Fei divided his forces into three columns. He sent a little over thirty men down the center to raid the camp and set it ablaze; the other two columns were ordered to circle behind the enemy camp and, when they saw the flames rise as the signal, attack from both sides. At the second watch, Zhang Fei personally led his picked troops to cut off Liu Dai's retreat; the thirty-odd men of the center column rushed into the camp and set it on fire. Just as Liu Dai's ambushing troops were about to charge in, Zhang Fei's two columns attacked together. Liu Dai's army fell into confusion. Having no idea how many troops Zhang Fei commanded, the men broke and scattered. Liu Dai led a band of his shattered troops away in search of an escape route, only to run straight into Zhang Fei; meeting on the narrow road, he found it impossible to evade him; and after a single exchange on horseback, Zhang Fei captured him alive. All the remaining troops surrendered.

p.src: Zhang Fei sent a man ahead to report the victory in Xuzhou. When Xuande heard the news, he said to Yunchang, “Yide has always been rough and impetuous, but now he has employed strategy as well. I need worry no longer.” He then went personally beyond the city walls to welcome him. Zhang Fei said, “Elder brother called me hot-tempered and violent. What do you say now?” Xuande said, “Had I not goaded you with those words, how would you ever have consented to use a stratagem?” Zhang Fei laughed heartily. When Xuande saw Liu Dai being brought forward in bonds, he hurriedly dismounted, untied him, and said, “My younger brother Zhang Fei has offended you through his reckless conduct. I beg your forgiveness.” He welcomed Liu Dai into Xuzhou, released Wang Zhong, and entertained them both with courtesy. Xuande said, “Previously, Che Zhou sought to kill me, and so I had no choice but to kill him. The Chancellor mistakenly suspects me of rebellion and has sent you two generals to call me to account. I have received great favor from the Chancellor and have been seeking only to repay his kindness. How would I dare rebel? When you two generals return to the capital at Xu, I beg you to speak well of me and explain my case. I would count it my great good fortune.” Liu Dai and Wang Zhong said, “We are deeply indebted to you, Imperial Uncle, for sparing our lives. We shall do what we can for you before the Chancellor, pledging the lives of both our families as your surety.”

p.src: Xuande thanked them. The next day, he returned all the troops and horses they had originally commanded and escorted them beyond the city walls. Liu Dai and Wang Zhong had gone little more than ten li when a drum sounded and Zhang Fei barred their way, roaring, “My elder brother has no sense at all! Why release enemy generals after capturing them?” Liu Dai and Wang Zhong trembled in their saddles with fright. Zhang Fei glared and charged at them with his spear leveled, but someone came galloping from behind and shouted, “Do not behave so outrageously!” They looked and saw that it was Yunchang. Only then did Liu Dai and Wang Zhong feel reassured. Yunchang said, “Since our elder brother has released them, how can you disobey his command?” Zhang Fei said, “Release them this time, and they will only come back again.” Yunchang replied, “If they come again, it will not be too late to kill them then.” Liu Dai and Wang Zhong repeatedly begged leave to depart, saying, “Even if the Prime Minister exterminates our three clans, we will never come again. We beg the general to forgive us.” Zhang Fei said, “Even if Cao Cao himself came, I would slaughter his forces to the last man! For now, I will merely leave these two heads on your shoulders and keep account of them!” Clutching their heads, Liu Dai and Wang Zhong scurried away like frightened rats. Yunchang and Yide returned to Xuande and said, “Cao Cao is certain to come again.” Sun Qian said to Xuande, “Xuzhou is a place exposed to enemy attack and cannot be occupied for long; it would be better to divide our forces between Xiaopei and the defense of Pi, forming mutually supporting positions against Cao Cao.” Xuande followed his counsel and ordered Yunchang to defend Xiapi; Madam Gan and Madam Mi were also settled in Xiapi: Madam Gan was a native of Xiaopei, while Madam Mi was Mi Zhu’s younger sister. Sun Qian, Jian Yong, Mi Zhu, and Mi Fang were left to defend Xuzhou. Xuande and Zhang Fei stationed themselves at Xiaopei.
